directAnswer: To unzip a file, right-click on the zipped file and select 'Extract All' or use a file extraction tool like WinRAR or 7-Zip.
summary: Unzipping files is a straightforward process that can be done using built-in tools on most operating systems or third-party software.

sections.heading: Unzipping on Windows
sections.body: On Windows, you can unzip files using the built-in File Explorer or third-party applications.

sections.heading: Unzipping on Mac
sections.body: On Mac, double-clicking the zipped file will automatically unzip it using the Archive Utility.

sections.heading: Unzipping on Linux
sections.body: On Linux, you can use the command line with the 'unzip' command or graphical tools like Archive Manager.

steps.title: Using Windows File Explorer
steps.detail: Right-click on the zipped file, select 'Extract All', choose the destination folder, and click 'Extract'.

steps.title: Using Mac Archive Utility
steps.detail: Double-click the zipped file, and it will automatically extract to the same location.

steps.title: Using Command Line on Linux
steps.detail: Open a terminal and run 'unzip <filename>.zip' to extract the files.

faqs.question: What if I can't find the 'Extract All' option?
faqs.answer: Ensure you are right-clicking on the zipped file; if the option is missing, you may need to install a file extraction tool.

faqs.question: Can I unzip files on my mobile device?
faqs.answer: Yes, many mobile apps are available for both Android and iOS that can unzip files.

faqs.question: What if the zipped file is corrupted?
faqs.answer: If the file is corrupted, it may not unzip correctly. You may need to re-download the file.

caveats: Some zipped files may be password protected, requiring a password to unzip.
